overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing matters beyond the June 27 executive session's purpose, withholding those minutes, and failing to announce minutes review results; other allegations were dismissed or untimely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed matters at its June 27 executive session beyond the stated purpose of hearing complaints against a public official.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons set forth in our determination in OML 2024-128, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it discussed matters during the June 27 executive session that did not fall within the purpose for which the executive session was called, or any other permissible purpose.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board did not meet in open session before convening in executive session on June 27.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board complied with the requirement to meet in open session prior to convening in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board did not state the purpose of the executive session when it voted to enter executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review any allegation that the Board failed to state the purpose for entering executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board prohibited recording of the June 27 executive session, a right held by the Purpose 1 subject.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint was filed on November 21.  Therefore, it is untimely as to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to make the June 27 executive session minutes available to the public in their entirety.
Complaint alleged the Board failed to announce in open session the results of its review of executive session minutes for continued non-disclosure.
allegations.key_passage: As the Board failed to announce the outcome of a review conducted at reasonable intervals, regardless of whether it actually conducted such a review, it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair deliberated outside a posted meeting by sending an unsigned July 6 letter to members noting significant differences with the Town Administrator.
allegations.key_passage: Because neither the complainant nor the Board has the subject letter in its possession, and both must rely on a newspaper's account of the letter (as we would), we find insufficient support for the complainant's claim that the Board deliberated outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the violations were intentional under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: There is no evidence that the Board acted here with deliberate ignorance of the law's requirement or had previously been advised of noncompliance on the grounds set out here.  Therefore, we do not find that the violations were intentional.

remedy: Release to the public the June 27 executive session minutes within 30 days, unredacted except for one paragraph on page 3 summarizing discussion of two complaints about the Town Administrator.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Board, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to release to the public the minutes of the June 27 executive session, in their entirety and without any redactions, with the exception of the single paragraph approximately halfway down page 3 summarizing the discussion of two complaints regarding the Town Administrator.
